req.title: PUT rejects payload ID mismatch
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the playerId in the path does not match the id in the PUT body.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} must return HTTP 400 when the squad_number in the path does not match the squad_number in the request body. The route handler checks `if player_model.squad_number != squad_number` and raises HTTPException(400). Tests must cover: (1) positive — matching IDs yield no 400; (2) negative — mismatched IDs yield exactly 400; (3) boundary — off-by-one mismatch (path=10, body=11 and path=10, body=9) to catch comparison-operator mutations. Decision-table coverage ensures both sides of the equality check are exercised. Mutation targets: the `!=` operator (could be mutated to `==`), the status code constant 400 (could be mutated to 404 or 422), and the field being compared (squad_number).

tests.name: test_put_matching_squad_number_does_not_return_400
preconditions: Player with squad_number=10 exists in the database (pre-loaded fixture)
FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with body containing squad_number=10 (matching path)
expected: Response status code is NOT 400 (mismatch guard is not triggered)
Response status code is 204 or 500 (not 400 — the mismatch branch is bypassed)
trace: R-PLAYER-011: when path and body squad_number match, the 400 branch must NOT fire
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_matching_squad_number_does_not_return_400():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Kabir",
        "middleName": "Mary",
        "lastName": "Reddy",
        "dateOfBirth": "1910-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 10,
        "position": "Right Winger",
        "abbrPosition": "DM",
        "team": "River Plate",
        "league": "Ligue 1",
        "starting11": False
    }
    r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code != 400, f"Expected no 400 on match, got {r.status_code}"
    assert r.status_code in (204, 500), f"Unexpected status {r.status_code}"

tests.name: test_put_mismatch_check_fires_before_404_lookup
preconditions: Squad number 999 does NOT exist in the database
FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/999 with body containing squad_number=888 (both path and body are non-existent, and they differ)
expected: Response status code is exactly 400 (mismatch guard fires before the 404 lookup)
Response is not 404 — proving the ordering: mismatch check precedes existence check
trace: R-PLAYER-011: DT — mismatch guard must short-circuit before DB lookup; non-existent path + mismatched body -> 400 not 404
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_mismatch_check_fires_before_404_lookup():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Ghost",
        "middleName": None,
        "lastName": "Player",
        "dateOfBirth": "2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 888,
        "position": "Goalkeeper",
        "abbrPosition": "GK",
        "team": "Unknown",
        "league": "Unknown",
        "starting11": False
    }
    r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/999", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 400, f"Expected 400 (mismatch before 404), got {r.status_code}"
    assert r.status_code != 404, "Mismatch guard must fire before existence check"
